'The Productivity-Reliability Paradox: Specification-Driven Governance for AI-Augmented Software Development', arXiv:2605.01160v1 (cs.SE), submitted 1 May 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01160. Sec 7.4 and Table 4. No GitHub primary source found for the numbers (checked github/spec-kit README, github.blog Spec Kit launch post).
source_tier: Preprint (not peer-reviewed). The pilot is first-party to this preprint, not GitHub. The lead's attribution to 'GitHub's Spec Kit pilot' is wrong: GitHub did not run or publish it.
access_status: Preprint: PDF fully read as text via pdftotext (Sec 7.4 to 7.4.5, Table 4). Abstract page read. github/spec-kit README, spec-driven.md, docs/quickstart.md and templates/commands/constitution.md fetched. GitHub blog launch post read via fetch summary only [uncertain] (not full text). Web search for the exact figures found no other source.
sponsor_and_incentive: Funding not stated in sections read [uncertain]. Single author; the paper advances a Specification Governance Model that Spec Kit is evaluated as an instance of, so author has an interest in a favourable result. exact_quotes: Sec 7.4: 'an illustrative pilot study of Spec Kit was conducted within three full-stack web development teams over a four-month period. The objective was not to produce a controlled experiment...'
Sec 7.4.1: 'Fourteen engineers participated across three long-running full-stack web projects.' (8 mid-level, 6 senior, juniors excluded; unnamed 'mid-sized software organisation')

Sec 7.4.3: 'While precise effect sizes cannot be claimed given the study's retrospective design and absence of a parallel control group, the approximate operational metrics observed during the two phases are reported in Table 4 to provide indicative magnitudes.'

Table 4 note: 'These figures are drawn from Git, CI/CD, and issue-tracking systems and developer self-reports. They are reported as approximate ranges rather than point estimates because the study was not instrumented as a controlled experiment. Temporal confounds (e.g. improving AI model capabilities during the study period) cannot be excluded.'

Sec 7.4.5: 'It involved only fourteen engineers across three projects within a single organisation, and thus cannot support claims of statistical generalisation.' and 'The absence of a parallel control group ... introduces the possibility that observed improvements are attributable to temporal confounds'

spec-kit README: '/speckit-constitution Create principles focused on code quality, testing, and maintainability.' and 'Create a constitution once per project and repeat the remaining steps for each feature.'

spec-driven.md: 'At the heart of SDD lies a constitution—a set of immutable principles that govern how specifications become code. The constitution (`memory/constitution.md`) acts as the architectural DNA of the system...'
templates/commands/constitution.md description: 'Create or update the project constitution from interactive or provided principle inputs.'
key_claims: Farrag reports a retrospective, within-team before/after pilot (2 months baseline, 2 months with Spec Kit) of 14 engineers in 3 projects in one unnamed organisation, concluding Spec Kit governance is operationally viable and effects are 'qualitative and indicative'. Spec Kit is a GitHub open-source toolkit; neither its README nor GitHub's launch post reports any measured outcomes (README only popularity stats; blog says 'less guesswork, fewer surprises, and higher-quality code' qualitatively). /speckit.constitution (now written /speckit-constitution in the README) is the first step of the flow: creates or updates the project's constitution (memory/constitution.md), a set of principles for code quality, testing and maintainability that later specify/plan/tasks steps are checked against; run once per project. The hypothetical dot form /speckit.constitution is used in the Farrag paper and older docs.
headline_figures: Median lead time per feature: 8-12 working days baseline to 6-9 working days with Spec Kit (Table 4). Matches the lead's numbers. Comparison is the same teams, earlier 2 months; no control group.
Code churn (lines reverted <2 weeks): 12-18% of changed lines to 6-10%. Matches the lead.

Also in Table 4: late-stage hotfixes per sprint 3-5 to 1-2 across projects; rollbacks per month 2-4 to 0-1; developer-reported confidence Likert 3.1 to 3.9 mean; spec/plan authoring overhead 45-90 min per medium feature.

Lead's statement 'GitHub's pilot' does not match: source is Farrag's preprint, not GitHub. Lead's 'cut' wording overstates: paper calls them indicative approximate ranges. 'Short-horizon churn' wording is from the paper.
sample_and_method: 14 engineers (8 mid-level 3-5 yrs, 6 senior), 3 projects (B2B SaaS React/Node; consumer Vue/Nuxt/NestJS; internal admin React/Go/Python), four months, retrospective before/after at team level. Data from Git, CI/CD, issue trackers plus self-reports, interviews and Likert questionnaires. Raw data, organisation and per-team numbers not published in the text read.
limitations: Stated: single organisation, 14 engineers, no parallel control group, retrospective instrumentation, self-reports, juniors excluded, temporal confounds like improving models. Visible: ranges not point estimates, no statistics, author-designed framework being validated by author, unnamed organisation so unverifiable, Spec Kit phase also included new process attention (Hawthorne effect), baseline vs intervention order not counterbalanced, spec authoring overhead may be omitted from lead time [uncertain].
what_a_leader_can_do: Weak evidence only. Source supports trying a short constitution plus spec/plan/tasks gate on medium and high-impact changes and measuring lead time, churn, hotfixes and authoring overhead against a concurrent control. It does not support claiming Spec Kit cuts review burden or lead time. Paper also says verification effort shifted earlier rather than disappeared. Do not cite the numbers as GitHub results; if used at all, attribute to a single-author preprint's uncontrolled pilot.
overlap_with_site_essays: Overlaps with The Verification Gap and Checking Isn't Catching (verification effort shifted earlier, 'verification tax' framing); and What It Takes to Trust Agent Output (constitution as a trust constraint). Little on Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part beyond reduced review cognitive overhead claim. Recommendation: drop as GitHub evidence; at most a hedged mention of the preprint.
